newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish 3-yr bond min price seen down at tender.
newsitem.headline: Polish 3-yr bond min price seen down at tender.

text.p: The minimum price of the Polish three-year index-linked bonds is expected to fall in low demand amounting to less than half of the Treasury's 700 million zloty treasury offer on Tuesday, analysts said.
They said an attractive minimum price for today's auction would be around 97.0, down from a minimum of 100.0 for similar three year bonds at the last primary auction in October 1996.

Analysts said banks would probably test much lower prices because the finance ministry has recently cut the public and subscription sales price of one-year bonds to 96.5 and 95.5 from 102.50 and 103.00 previously. @
"Banks are likely to be cautious not to buy the paper worse than what will be offered to the public," said Grzegorz Raupuk, bond dealer at Bank Gdanski SA
These three-year bonds, due on February 6, 2000, go on public sale from February 3, 1997 but, like the one-year bonds, are no longer tax-deductable to individuals.
The value date for this auction is February 3, 1997.
